evidence: US Treasury OFAC press release sb0598 dated Aug 7 2026 announces sanctions on cryptocurrency exchanges and a network funding the Iranian IRGC under counterterrorism authorities, announced before the Aug 12 deadline.
disconfirming: Reuters reported Aug 5 2026 that Treasury delisted three IRGC-linked aviation entities that week, which does not negate the new Aug 7 designations.
note: Designations target IRGC funding networks rather than the already fully designated Corps itself, which is how new IRGC sanctions rounds are implemented; flagged in case the adjudicator reads on-the-IRGC hyper-literally.

evidence: BLS JOLTS for June 2026, released Aug 4 2026, put the national quits rate at 2.0 percent; BLS scheduled the July 2026 JOLTS for Sept 1 2026, so no report covering July existed by the Aug 12 deadline.
disconfirming: none found
note: Fails on two independent grounds: the deadline-era release covered June not July, and the published rate was 2.0 not 1.8.

evidence: Bloomberg reported Brent settled near 97 dollars on Fri Jul 24 2026 after a roughly 4 percent drop, implying a Jul 23 settlement near 101 after Brent topped 100 that week; Fortune daily trackers show Brent at 90.43 on Jul 27, about 92.65 around Jul 30 and 92.27 on Jul 31 before easing through August.
disconfirming: The Fortune figures are morning spot quotes rather than official ICE settlements, and the full ICE settlement series was not directly inspected.
note: At least three weekdays in the window very likely settled above 90 (Jul 23, Jul 24, plus late-July recovery days); adjudicator should confirm against ICE or EIA official settlement data.

evidence: Reuters, Moscow Times, Meduza and Euronews dated Aug 3 2026 report the beach drone strike that killed six to seven people, including three children, occurred at Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik in Krasnodar Krai on the Russian mainland; officials in Crimea reported four killed there that night, not at a beach.
disconfirming: A roughly seven-fatality beach strike is well sourced, including hostile-side acknowledgment of the incident, but it attaches to a mainland beach rather than Crimea.
note: Fails the geographic element as written: the deadly beach strike was in Krasnodar Krai, not Crimea, and the Crimea toll was four; outlets also split between six and seven dead at the beach.

evidence: The Bug Fire that ignited Aug 8 2026 on the California-Nevada line forced mass evacuations in Washoe County Nevada; the county emergency site reported roughly 3,800 households evacuated by Aug 9 and major outlets including Newsweek described thousands of people evacuated, inside the Aug 3-10 window.
disconfirming: The official figure counts households rather than persons, and the reporting agency is a county rather than a state emergency management agency.
note: Resolves on the major-news-outlet disjunct: thousands-evacuated reporting plus 3,800 households clears 1,000 people; a strict reading demanding a state-agency per-person count would not be satisfied.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-01: the six to seven beach deaths of Aug 3 2026 were at Arkhipo-Osipovka in Krasnodar Krai on the mainland per Reuters, Moscow Times and Meduza; Crimea itself recorded four deaths, not at a beach.
disconfirming: A fatality count near seven exists but at a mainland location.
note: Same geographic failure as KKR-20260804-01.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-03: Washoe County Nevada reported roughly 3,800 households evacuated for the Bug Fire by Aug 9 2026 and major outlets described thousands of people evacuated within the window.
disconfirming: The official count is in households and comes from a county rather than a state agency.
note: Same resolution as KKR-20260804-03 via the major-news-outlet disjunct.

evidence: Late July and early August 2026 reporting shows Romania responded to drone incursions bilaterally: ambassador summoned, protest note to Russia, a Russian diplomat expelled; the only Romanian UNSC protest letter located is S/2026/447 dated May 29 2026, and searches surface no new letter published in the UN document system between Aug 10 and Aug 13.
disconfirming: UN document indexing lags and is imperfectly searchable, so a letter could exist unindexed, but no press or UN reference to one was found.
note: Criterion requires a specific instrument in a narrow three-day window; absence after targeted searching scores MISS, with residual uncertainty from UN indexing lag.

evidence: A GlobalSecurity daily log dated Aug 12 2026 states no US or Israeli strike inside Iran was confirmed by CENTCOM from the cancellation of a threatened campaign late Aug 1 through Aug 12, a thirteenth consecutive quiet night; the last CENTCOM-confirmed strike wave on Iran completed Jul 29, one day before this window opened.
disconfirming: Coverage dated Aug 13 and 14 centered on stalled diplomacy, economic pressure and maritime attacks, with no wire or CENTCOM report of a new strike on Iranian soil.
note: The operational log runs to Aug 12; the final window day Aug 13 is covered only by absence of any strike report in extensive news coverage, which an adjudicator may wish to reconfirm.

evidence: Kurdistan24 and Bol News reported that Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the Khazina Banda police post attack in Hangu via a video statement circulated on social media within days of the assault; Pakistani police attributed the attack to the banned group officials label Khawarij, the state term for TTP.
disconfirming: Initial AP and Al Jazeera coverage on Jul 30 said no group had immediately claimed responsibility.
note: Turns on whether Kurdistan24 or Bol News counts as a major outlet reporting the claim; the wire services did not carry the claim in results reviewed, so source weight is the open question for the adjudicator.

evidence: Rapid7, Arctic Wolf, Huntress and CISA KEV materials from early Aug 2026 confirm CVE-2026-18577 in N-able N-central was exploited in the wild against MSP and enterprise environments, but no federal agency, CISA advisory or major outlet identified a resulting breach of a US critical infrastructure system in the Aug 4-11 window.
disconfirming: Huntress confirmed at least one victim organization; none was identified as critical infrastructure.
note: Active exploitation is confirmed; the specific critical-infrastructure breach element is what fails.

evidence: Axios and CNBC dated Aug 4-5 2026 reported the US, Iran and Oman were nearing an interim Hormuz arrangement, and ABC reported messages exchanged through intermediaries; Iranian state-carried remarks by FM Araghchi around Aug 8 said negotiations with the US could not resume, and no official launch of a bilateral dialogue was announced in the window.
disconfirming: Indirect and trilateral contacts were extensively reported, but nothing meeting the official-launch and one-outlet-per-country requirement.
note: The Oman-mediated track is not the formal bilateral dialogue launch the criterion demands.

evidence: The Hacker News, Resecurity and incident trackers show INC Ransomware highly active in late July and early Aug 2026 with government and private victims, but no CISA advisory or pair of outlets ties INC to a breach affecting more than 50,000 US government employees in the Aug 4-11 window.
disconfirming: none found
note: INC is also not new; it has operated since 2023, contrary to the claim framing.

evidence: CBS, Axios, NPR and The Hill dated Aug 3 2026 report the House Ethics Committee recommended censure of Rep. Chuck Edwards and said it would offer a privileged resolution; the House stood in recess until Aug 31, so no censure was enacted in the Aug 4-11 window.
disconfirming: Edwards moved to end his reelection campaign, but no floor censure vote occurred.
note: A committee recommendation on Aug 3 is neither a formal censure nor inside the window; the floor vote was expected after the House returns Aug 31.

evidence: Washington Post, CNN, NPR and NBC report the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as Attorney General early Saturday Aug 8 2026 by a vote of 50-49.
disconfirming: none found; the 50-49 tally is consistent across outlets
note: The confirmation occurred inside the window but the compound criterion fails on the 60-vote margin element.

evidence: The large digital-asset theft in the period was the Coldcard hardware wallet compromise, reported around early Aug 2026 at roughly 100 to 130 million dollars in bitcoin, but Coldcard maker Coinkite is a Canadian wallet vendor, not a US financial institution; Reuters-cited reporting on breaches at Blackstone, Moodys and CME described data theft and extortion, not a nine-figure digital-asset theft.
disconfirming: The Coldcard loss exceeds the 100 million dollar threshold but fails the victim-class element.
note: No event pairs a US financial institution with over 100 million dollars in stolen digital assets inside the window.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-02: CVE-2026-18577 exploitation in the wild is confirmed by Rapid7, Huntress and CISA KEV materials, but no source identifies a resulting breach of a US critical infrastructure system in the Aug 4-11 window.
disconfirming: At least one victim organization is confirmed by Huntress, none identified as critical infrastructure.
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-02.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-04: Aug 4-5 reporting by Axios and CNBC describes a near-final trilateral Hormuz arrangement via Oman, while Iranian officials publicly ruled out resumed talks with the US; no official launch of a bilateral dialogue was announced in the window.
disconfirming: Extensive indirect-contact reporting exists but nothing satisfying the launch-plus-one-outlet-per-country requirement.
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-04.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-05: INC Ransomware activity in the window is documented, but no CISA advisory or two outlets confirm a breach affecting more than 50,000 US government employees.
disconfirming: none found
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-05.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-06: the Ethics Committee recommendation of censure came Aug 3 and the House remained in recess until Aug 31, so no formal censure occurred in the window.
disconfirming: none found beyond the pre-window committee recommendation
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-06.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-07: Blanche was confirmed Aug 8 2026 by 50-49, short of 60.
disconfirming: none found
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-07; fails on the vote margin.

evidence: Duplicate of KKR-20260804-08: the qualifying-scale theft was the Coldcard wallet compromise of roughly 100 to 130 million dollars in bitcoin, and Coinkite is a Canadian wallet vendor rather than a US financial institution.
disconfirming: The Coldcard loss clears the dollar threshold but not the victim-class element.
note: Same finding as KKR-20260804-08.

evidence: Weathernews and The Watchers coverage of Typhoon Dolphin, which passed near Okinawa around Aug 7 2026 at about 935 hPa, documents JMA typhoon warnings and advisories including violent wind and storm surge warnings, with no mention of a Special Warning, the highest JMA tier, in the Aug 4-11 window.
disconfirming: Coverage of the storm was detailed enough that a Special Warning would likely have been reported; none was found.
note: Verdict rests on absence of any Special Warning reference in detailed storm coverage; the JMA advisory archive itself was not inspected.

evidence: Same price path as KKR-20260722-09 over a window extended to Aug 14: Bloomberg-reported settlements near 101 and 97 on Jul 23-24 and Fortune tracker readings of 90.43 to 92.65 across Jul 27-31 give three or more weekdays above 90.
disconfirming: Aug 1-14 added no qualifying days, with Brent fading to roughly 87-88 by Aug 14; the daily figures are spot quotes rather than official ICE settlements.
note: Resolution rides entirely on the late-July days; adjudicator should confirm exact ICE settlements for Jul 23, 24, 29 and 30.

evidence: Market coverage shows WTI peaked near 92 to 93.45 dollars in late July 2026 before a Jul 27 selloff of more than seven percent, and traded in the 80s thereafter; no CME front-month settlement at or above 95 between Jul 27 and Aug 14 appears in any reviewed source.
disconfirming: none found
note: The late-July WTI peak fell short of 95 and occurred at or before Jul 24, outside the window; the full CME settlement series was not directly inspected.

evidence: Bloomberg reported Brent retreated from 100 dollars and settled near 97 on Jul 24 2026, before the window opened; within Jul 27 to Aug 14 the highest observed Brent levels were around 92 to 93 in late July per Fortune trackers, fading to 87-88 by mid August, with no settlement at or above 100.
disconfirming: Brent traded near or briefly above 100 in the week ending Jul 24, but that predates the window.
note: The 100 threshold was approached only before Jul 27; within the window Brent never settled near 100.

evidence: The named army.mil article, retrieved via search cache and corroborated by DVIDS coverage from mid June 2026, names Lt. Gen. Gregory Anderson as commanding general of XVIII Airborne Corps in its text about the senior enlisted adviser change, and no reporting indicates a corps change of command before Aug 14 2026.
disconfirming: Direct live fetch of the page returned rate-limit errors, so the Aug 14 reading relies on cached copies of a static article.
note: The article is a static June 2026 piece that names Anderson; a hit required a different officer to be named, so this scores MISS.

evidence: A DPA wire dated Jul 26 2026, carried by Freie Presse, Onvista and others, reports Justice Minister Hubig announced the Generalbundesanwalt would take over the Berlin CSD vehicle attack investigation as a suspected Islamist terror attack; the German Wikipedia article on the attack documents federal terror proceedings and an Islamic State pledge video attributed to the attacker, all well before Aug 14.
disconfirming: Of the three named agencies only DPA reporting was directly verified in results; DW and Reuters coverage and a Generalbundesanwalt website statement were not independently captured.
note: Substantively the terror classification and GBA takeover are beyond doubt; formally the criterion wants a GBA statement or two of DPA, DW and Reuters, and only DPA was verified here, which an adjudicator can complete easily.

evidence: A CENTCOM public release dated Jul 29 2026, titled US Strikes IRGC Targets After Attempted Iranian Attacks, states CENTCOM forces completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran at 10 pm ET on Jul 29 in response to attempted Iranian missile attacks on US forces; Jul 29 falls inside the Jul 28 to Aug 14 window and CENTCOM confirmation satisfies the first disjunct.
disconfirming: Strikes then paused: a daily log dated Aug 12 records no further confirmed US strikes inside Iran after the campaign cancellation late Aug 1.
note: Window opens Jul 28 and therefore captures the CENTCOM-confirmed Jul 29 strike wave; contrast KKR-20260730-21, whose Jul 30 window excludes it and correctly scores MISS.

evidence: Japan Times dated Aug 8 2026, citing the Kumamoto prefectural disaster headquarters, put the toll from the Jul 28 Kumamoto quake at 39; earlier prefectural figures were 38 on Aug 3, and no source reports a toll above 40, let alone above 50, by Aug 14.
disconfirming: Two deaths remained under investigation for quake linkage, insufficient to reach 50 even if confirmed.
note: The Jul 28 Kyushu quake is the same M6.8 Uto-Kumamoto event referenced in KKR-20260730-24; the criterion names FDMA or Cabinet Office figures and the widely cited counts are prefectural, but all official counts sit far below 50.

evidence: Japan Times dated Aug 8 2026 reports 39 dead in the M6.8 Uto-Kumamoto earthquake per prefectural authorities, including direct and disaster-related deaths; no Japanese government, NHK or wire report above 40 was found through Aug 14.
disconfirming: Two further deaths were under investigation; if both were certified the toll would reach 41, but no such report exists in the window.
note: A narrow miss: confirmed toll of 39 against a threshold of above 40.

evidence: Al Jazeera dated Aug 8 2026, carrying Reuters and AP reporting, states the UAE accused Iran of striking an ADNOC tanker with a missile in the Strait of Hormuz early Aug 8, and ADNOC said three of its vessels were attacked that week; this is a new Iran-linked strike on a vessel reported by the named wires inside the Jul 31 to Aug 14 window.
disconfirming: ADNOC itself did not name the attacker; the Iran attribution came from the UAE government and Gulf states.
note: The wire-service disjunct is satisfied; attribution rests on UAE statements, which the Iran-linked phrasing of the criterion accommodates.

evidence: The CISA alert adding CVE-2026-9198 to the KEV catalog is dated Aug 4 2026 in the advisory URL and text, and NVD records per Windows Forum carry an Aug 4 addition date with an Aug 7 remediation deadline; the criterion requires a date-added between Aug 5 and Aug 12.
disconfirming: The Hacker News and a KEVIntel prose passage give Aug 5 2026 as the addition date, which would fall inside the window, but the primary CISA advisory and NVD say Aug 4.
note: Turns entirely on a one-day boundary: primary sources put date-added at Aug 4, one day before the window opens; an adjudicator relying on the Hacker News date would flip this to HIT, so pulling the dateAdded field from the KEV JSON is worth the check.

evidence: USGS event records and AFP-carried reporting show a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck about 32 km southwest of Sarangani, Mindanao, Philippines on Aug 5 2026 at roughly 10 km depth, prompting a green PAGER alert; magnitude, depth, location and date all satisfy the criterion.
disconfirming: EMSC listed a 35 km depth estimate, still far under the 100 km ceiling.
note: Inclusion in the USGS significant-quakes feed specifically was not inspected, but a shallow M6.3 near populated Mindanao with a PAGER product is the class of event that feed carries.
